Worked Example: Setting a Calorie Target

A 35-year-old woman who is 5'6" and 150 lb with light exercise needs about 1,914 calories a day to maintain her weight (Mifflin-St Jeor with a 1.375 activity factor). A 500-calorie daily deficit would put her near 1,414.

Rule of thumb: about 3,500 calories equals one pound of body fat, so a 500-calorie daily deficit points to roughly one pound per week. Real results vary, and the rate usually slows over time.

Safe Limits

Very low calorie intakes can cause nutrient gaps and muscle loss, and are best done under medical supervision. As a general guide, many calculators and clinicians avoid recommending targets below about 1,200 calories for women or 1,500 for men without supervision. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, adolescence and medical conditions change the numbers, so check with a clinician.

Getting More From the Number

  • Pair calories with protein, carbs and fat using the macro calculator.
  • See how exercise changes the picture with the calories burned calculator.
  • Check your starting point with the BMI calculator.

extra_faqs.q: How many calories should I eat a day to lose weight?
extra_faqs.a: Start from your maintenance calories and subtract a moderate amount, commonly 250 to 500 per day. Avoid cutting too low, and check with a clinician if you have health conditions.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to eat back exercise calories?
extra_faqs.a: Many activity multipliers already include typical exercise. If you add extra workouts beyond your chosen activity level, you may need slightly more food.

extra_faqs.q: Why have I stopped losing weight?
extra_faqs.a: As weight falls, maintenance calories fall too. Recalculate with your new weight and review your intake and activity.
